gloss: one after another; in succession; continuously

definitions.explanation: Describing things or people arriving or happening in continuous sequence.

examples.japanese: ⟦{参加者|さんかしゃ}→参加者：03059_sankasha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{集|あつ}まって→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧⟦きた→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
⟦{新商品|しんしょうひん}→新商品：11504_shinshouhin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{続々|ぞくぞく}⟦{発売|はつばい}されている→発売：04315_hatsubai⟧。
examples.english: New products are being released in succession.

examples.japanese: ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{発覚|はっかく}した→発覚：07629_hakkaku⟧。
examples.english: Problems came to light one after another.

examples.japanese: ⟦{国内|こくない}→国内：02998_kokunai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{応募|おうぼ}→応募：03014_oubo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{届|とど}いた→届く：00899_todoku⟧。
examples.english: Applications from around the country arrived one after another.

examples.japanese: ⟦{被災地|ひさいち}→被災地：27434_hisaichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{支援|しえん}→支援：07778_shien⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{集|あつ}まった→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: Aid arrived one after another in the disaster-stricken area.

notes:
{続々|ぞくぞく} is an adverb describing continuous succession or sequence, often used with the particle ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{集|あつ}まる→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧ (to gather in succession)
- {続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{届|とど}く→届く：00899_todoku⟧ (to arrive one after another)
- {続々|ぞくぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{発表|はっぴょう}される→発表：03562_happyou⟧ (to be announced in succession)

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
ぞくぞく can also be written as ⟦{族々|ぞくぞく}→族々：noentry⟧ (rare) or in hiragana ぞくぞく meaning "to shiver" or "to be thrilled." Context usually makes the meaning clear:
- {続々|ぞくぞく}: Succession (written with {続})
- ⟦ぞくぞく→ぞくぞく：noentry⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: To shiver, feel chills, or feel thrilled (usually hiragana)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {続々|ぞくぞく} vs. ⟦{次々|つぎつぎ}→次々：03522_tsugitsugi⟧: Both mean "one after another," but ⟦{次々|つぎつぎ}→次々：03522_tsugitsugi⟧ emphasizes the sequential order, while {続々|ぞくぞく} emphasizes continuous flow.

Register: Neutral. Used in both formal and casual contexts.
